about: The model's tools. The server offers the enabled ones to the model; the browser runs them. One source for both: a contract test checks that the browser runs exactly the enabled tools. A tool is enabled once the browser can run it.
guidance: Use your tools whenever data, calculation or a visual would make the answer better. Look at the data before you draw conclusions, and check your own output when a tool reports back.

tools.name: run_js
tools.description: Run JavaScript (top-level await allowed) in a sandbox with no network. Available: fs.readFile(name) and fs.readdir() for this chat's files (PDF and Word arrive as text), sql(query) for DuckDB over CSV, Excel and Parquet files, d3, and a document object so ordinary d3 code produces SVG or HTML. You get back the value of a top-level return statement and anything written with console.log.

tools.name: render_html
tools.description: Show the user a page you wrote: a whole HTML document or a fragment, with its scripts running and d3 available. There is no network. You get back any errors and a short summary of what appeared, so you can check your work.

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetch a web page or file and get it back as readable text. The user may be asked to approve the request first.
